title: Restriction of a derived Chow transform on an algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived pullback and tensor use K-flat resolutions; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and of finite presentation (diagonal a closed immersion, and quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale charts), and put $P=\mathbf P^n_A$ for $n\geq0$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Let $h:Z\hookrightarrow T=X\times_A P$ be a closed immersion, write $p:T\to X$ and $q:T\to P$ for the projections, and put $b=p\circ h$ and $c=q\circ h$. Let $V\subset P$ be open, set $W=c^{-1}(V)$, and suppose that $j=c|_W:W\hookrightarrow V$ is a closed immersion and $b_W=b|_W:W\to X$ is etale. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_T)$ satisfy $E|_{X\times_A V}\simeq(h_*\mathcal O_Z)[0]|_{X\times_A V}$. For every $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_V)$, $$\left(Rq_*(Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_T}E)\right)|_V\simeq Rj_*(b_W^*K).$$ Here $W$ is a scheme because it is closed in $V$, and the etale restriction $b_W^*K$ equals $Lb_W^*K$.

source.place: Tag 0CTS, lemma-compute-Fourier-Mukai-for-derived-chow, displayed derived isomorphism and proof (using only its stated kernel restriction and etaleness hypotheses).

proof.text: Put $T_V=X\times_A V$, with $a:T_V\to T$, $p_V:T_V\to X$ and $q_V:T_V\to V$. The inverse image $Z\times_TT_V$ equals $c^{-1}(V)=W$; write $i:W\to T_V$. Then $p_Vi=b_W$ and $q_Vi=j$. The closed-subspace definition makes $i$ a representable closed immersion: on every scheme test its fibre product is the same scheme test of $h$. On an affine chart a closed immersion is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence affine and quasi-compact; its diagonal is an isomorphism, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus $i$ is qcqs. Likewise the given representable closed immersion $j$ into the scheme $V$ makes $W$ a scheme.

Apply etale localization of total direct image to $q$ and the open immersion $V\to P$. For $B=Lp^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}E$ this gives $(Rq_*B)|_V\simeq R(q_V)_*(B|_{T_V})$. Restriction is exact and preserves K-flat complexes, so restricting K-flat representatives for the two factors computes the restricted derived tensor. Derived pullback composition along $a$ and $p$, with $La^*=a^*$ since $a$ is etale, identifies $(Lp^*K)|_{T_V}$ with $Lp_V^*K$. Consequently $B|_{T_V}\simeq Lp_V^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}(E|_{T_V})$.

The degree-zero direct-image restriction comparison applied to $h$ and $a$ gives $(h_*\mathcal O_Z)|_{T_V}\simeq i_*\mathcal O_W$. Using the specified kernel isomorphism, the complex inside $R(q_V)_*$ is therefore $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}(i_*\mathcal O_W)[0]$, where $L=Lp_V^*K$. Derived pullback preserves quasi-coherent cohomology, so $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{T_V})$. The structure module $\mathcal O_W$ is quasi-coherent, having the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_W\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_W\to0$ in the local-presentation definition.

The small ringed-site module category on $W$ is Grothendieck and has enough injectives. Choose an injective resolution $\mathcal O_W[0]\to I^\bullet$ concentrated in nonnegative degrees. It is K-injective by the bounded-below injective-complex theorem, so $i_*I^\bullet$ represents $Ri_*\mathcal O_W[0]$. Since $i$ is affine and $\mathcal O_W$ is quasi-coherent, affine module higher-image vanishing gives $H^r(i_*I^\bullet)=0$ for $r>0$. Negative degrees vanish because the complex is zero there. Left exactness of module direct image identifies $H^0(i_*I^\bullet)$ with $i_*\mathcal O_W$. Thus the augmentation $(i_*\mathcal O_W)[0]\to i_*I^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, giving the canonical natural identification $(i_*\mathcal O_W)[0]\simeq Ri_*\mathcal O_W[0]$.

Apply the unbounded qcqs algebraic-space projection formula to $i$, $F=\mathcal O_W[0]$ and $L=Lp_V^*K$. Step 1 checks qcqs and Step 3 checks both quasi-coherence hypotheses. With tensor symmetry and the structure-module unit this gives $L\otimes^{\mathbf L}Ri_*\mathcal O_W[0]\simeq Ri_*(\mathcal O_W[0]\otimes^{\mathbf L}Li^*L)\simeq Ri_*Li^*L$. Substituting Step 4 into Steps 2 and 3 now identifies the required left side with $R(q_V)_*Ri_*Li^*Lp_V^*K$.

Derived pullback composition gives $Li^*Lp_V^*K\simeq L(p_Vi)^*K=Lb_W^*K$, while derived direct-image composition gives $R(q_V)_*Ri_*\simeq R(q_Vi)_*=Rj_*$. Finally $b_W$ is etale by hypothesis, so its tensor pullback is exact slice restriction and $Lb_W^*K\simeq b_W^*K$. This yields $Rj_*(b_W^*K)$ in $D(\mathcal O_V)$. Localization, the fixed kernel isomorphism tensored with $K$, the projection formula, and the composition comparisons are natural in $K$, so their composite is the claimed natural isomorphism.
